ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Pulmonology (sarcoidosis) Referral — Mahalia Jackson

code.originalText: Three months of breathlessness, cough, tiredness and palpitations in a touring singer of 52: examination, chest radiograph, ECG and blood tests

text.paragraph: Suspected sarcoidosis in a 52-year-old gospel singer with three months of exertional breathlessness, dry cough, tiredness and chest tightness, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy with upper-zone reticulonodular opacities on today's chest radiograph, a calcium of 10.8 mg/dL, lymphopenia, and palpitations with first-degree atrioventricular block and frequent ventricular ectopy on ECG. Granulomas were reported at an abdominal operation twelve years ago; no pathology report is available. Please see her within two weeks, obtain tissue, and advise on cardiac evaluation and treatment. [S]
Urgency: Urgent, within two weeks; tissue sampling can be arranged before the visit. [S]

list.item: Is this sarcoidosis, and what is needed to confirm it and exclude tuberculosis, fungal infection and lymphoma?
Which other organs should be screened, and how should her high calcium and vitamin D be handled?
Does she have cardiac sarcoidosis, and what tests should be done, and in what order relative to any treatment?
Does she need treatment, and with what, including a steroid-sparing agent?
What is her risk of dangerous heart rhythms, and does she need a defibrillator or pacemaker?
How should treatment be monitored and its side effects prevented, and how can she keep singing and touring?

text.paragraph: Three months of breathlessness on one flight of stairs and on stage, a dry cough, tiredness, and tightness in the chest; she cannot hold long phrases and has shortened her concerts. Two spells of palpitations with light-headedness while singing; no fainting. At 40, after a concert tour abroad during which she was breathless and had abdominal cramps, she had a hysterectomy, and granulomas were reported in her abdomen; she was told she had sarcoidosis. Takes an over-the-counter calcium and vitamin D tablet, stopped today; no other medicines; no known allergies. Never smoker; no alcohol; no known exposure to birds, mold, metals or tuberculosis. Examination: oxygen saturation 95 percent, irregular pulse with ectopic beats, clear chest, no rash, no palpable nodes. Results today: chest radiograph as above; ECG PR 240 ms with ventricular ectopics; hemoglobin 12.4 g/dL, lymphocytes 0.9; calcium 10.8 mg/dL; creatinine 1.08 mg/dL; alkaline phosphatase 128 U/L; 25-hydroxyvitamin D 22 ng/mL and 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D 84 pg/mL; NT-proBNP 210 pg/mL; TSH 1.8; A1c 5.9%. Interferon-gamma release assay and HIV test sent; CT of the chest booked this week. She tours and records for her living and wants a plan she can keep [S]

list.item: Short of breath on stairs and on stage for about three months, with a dry cough, tiredness and tightness in the chest; she runs out of breath in the middle of long phrases; twice her heart has raced and she felt faint while singing. [S]

She was told after an operation twelve years ago that she had sarcoidosis; no record of that operation is available to this clinic, and she wants a clear answer and a plan that a working singer can keep. [S]
Her spring concerts and recording sessions are booked; she does not want to cancel unless she has to, and she needs her voice. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Mahalia Jackson was born in New Orleans on October 26, 1911, the third of six children of a man who was a longshoreman by day, a barber by night and a clergyman on Sunday. Her mother died when she was six, and she was raised by an aunt in a poor but respectable home; she left school in the eighth grade to work as a cook and washerwoman. [D]

In 1928 she moved to Chicago, worked as a hotel maid and laundress, and joined the Greater Salem Baptist Church, where she became a soloist. She never learned to read music. After her Carnegie Hall debut on October 4, 1950, she began touring abroad in 1952, and toured widely for the rest of her life. [D]

She was closely associated with the civil rights movement and sang at the March on Washington in 1963 before Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.'s speech. When she moved into an all-white neighborhood on the South Side of Chicago, a bullet was fired through a window of her home. [D]

Touring the segregated South for as many as 200 dates a year, she and her company had trouble finding safe places to sleep, eat and buy gas, sometimes slept in her car, lived on bags of fruit and drove half the night, and she arrived so exhausted she was almost dizzy when she sang; she insisted on being paid in cash because checks were often refused. [D]

Before and during her first European tour in 1952 she had difficulty breathing during and after performances and severe abdominal cramping, sang many shows in pain, lost a great deal of weight and finally cancelled the tour. On her return she had a hysterectomy, at which numerous granulomas were found in her abdomen, and she was diagnosed with sarcoidosis. From then on she had occasional bouts of fatigue and shortness of breath that became more frequent as her schedule filled. [D]

Diagnosis of suspected sarcoidosis: chest radiograph and CT of the chest, tissue by EBUS-guided needle aspiration rather than mediastinoscopy, stains and cultures for mycobacteria and fungi, an interferon-gamma release assay and HIV test to exclude other causes; serum ACE is not used to make or exclude the diagnosis. Guideline: Crouser ED, et al. Diagnosis and Detection of Sarcoidosis. An Official American Thoracic Society Clinical Practice Guideline. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2020;201(8):e26-e51 (PMID 32293205) (2020) [S]

Screening every patient with suspected sarcoidosis for other organ involvement: ECG, serum calcium with 25-hydroxyvitamin D and 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, creatinine, liver tests and alkaline phosphatase, complete blood count, TSH, and an eye examination; stop the calcium and vitamin D supplement while calcium is high. Guideline: Crouser ED, et al. Diagnosis and Detection of Sarcoidosis. An Official American Thoracic Society Clinical Practice Guideline. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2020;201(8):e26-e51 (PMID 32293205) (2020) [S]
